PullRequest.Title: chat: add a text-only /automate tip
PullRequest.Body:

## Motivation

The Agents window's chat tips don't mention `/automate`. This PR adds a text-only tip suggesting it for turning a task into a recurring automation with the agent, behind a default-off setting.

<details>
<summary>Code stats</summary>

- 4 files changed, +61/-0.
- Tip registration: +17.
- Setting registration and identifier: +8.
- Focused test: +36.

</details>

## Changes made

- Add: "Use `/automate` to have the agent walk you through turning a task into a recurring automation."
- Add `chat.automateTip.enabled`, defaulting to `false`, with `experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`.
- Show the enabled tip only in the Agents window with chat and automations enabled, and exclude it after the automation configuration tool is used.
- Keep `/automate` non-clickable. No insertion command or built-in skill changes.
- Cover the setting and existing eligibility conditions in the chat-tip tests.

<details>
<summary>Validation</summary>

- `corepack pnpm run build-fast --client-only`: passed.
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\chatTipService.test.ts --reporter dot`: 119 passed.
- `corepack pnpm run oxlint src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\common\constants.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\chat.shared.contribution.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\chatTipCatalog.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\chatTipService.test.ts`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Typecheck and live UI validation were not rerun for the setting change.

To try it manually, enable `chat.automateTip.enabled` in the Agents window with chat and automations enabled, then navigate to the `/automate` tip. Disable the setting to exclude it.

</details>

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup resolves the new experimental `chat.automateTip.enabled` default.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ConfigurationDefaultOverridesContribution scans experimental properties and awaits treatment resolution before reloading defaults; extension registration is also awaited independently. The added property contributes one treatment lookup to that existing startup pass.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the experiment treatment from the shared TAS assignments client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional treatment-name read, but TAS client initialization/fetch is shared and coalesced across all experimental settings; it does not create one network request per setting. Cold startup performs the existing shared assignment fetch, while warm reads use the client's cached assignment payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Startup already initialized and awaited the shared assignments client for many existing experimental settings; this diff adds one name read without adding another transport fetch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The treatment read is awaited by the existing defaults-update pass, but after the shared payload resolves its marginal work is a cached variable lookup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of registered experimental settings grows by exactly one; refetch work likewise grows by one constant-time treatment read.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Experimental properties are processed sequentially, while all names share the same TAS client and cached assignment payload; there is no new request fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold startup shares one in-flight assignments fetch across treatment reads. Warm/refetch reads resolve from the client assignment payload; no new cache key with independent transport or negative-cache retry loop is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: configuration processing and assignment-client code directly show one added lookup backed by a shared TAS client.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact cached lookup latency is unmeasured, but the added cardinality is fixed at one and no extra network request is created.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff adds bounded cached work to an existing startup pass, not a new network boundary or scaling fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents window evaluates, selects, and renders chat tips, including the new `/automate` tip.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When the tip lane becomes visible or a relevant configuration context key changes, ChatInputTipPresenter asks ChatTipService for a welcome tip; the service filters the static catalog and renders only the selected tip. The new entry adds one eligibility check and only constructs its short MarkdownString if selected or command validation reaches it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List prompt and agent instruction files for tips with file-based exclusions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged: only catalog entries with `excludeWhenPromptFilesExist` are checked, and the added tip has no such exclusion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same pre-existing file-exclusion tips triggered the same coalesced per-tip checks before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These asynchronous checks remain independent of selecting the new tip and are not added to its render critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the selected tip ID to application storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing store per newly selected welcome tip; adding a catalog candidate does not increase stores per selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A selected catalog tip already caused exactly one LastTipId store.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after selection on the existing path; the diff can change which ID is stored but not operation count.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Catalog size increases by one fixed entry. Each selection/navigation scan performs at most one extra context-expression and exclusion check; no user-controlled collection multiplies the added work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Tip filtering and rendering are synchronous on one UI event. There are no subprocess, IPC, database, or network calls on the added tip's selection/render path; only one tip is rendered.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The selected tip is retained for stable rerenders, so unchanged rerenders do not rebuild or rotate it. Dismissed and invoked-tool state is read from existing in-memory sets after startup storage restoration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: catalog filtering, stable-selection caching, and presenter rendering are directly visible in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: DOM/markdown render time is unmeasured, but the added text is short and only one tip is rendered, making the mechanism bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: one constant-size catalog entry adds negligible bounded CPU/allocation and no new expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Automation configuration tool invocation updates eligibility so the `/automate` tip is no longer offered.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: TipEligibilityTracker's existing tool listener checks an in-memory pending-tools set on tool invocations. When `vscode_configureAutomation` is first observed, it updates sets and persists invoked-tool IDs; subsequent invocations no longer perform that write for this ID.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and store the invoked-tool ID set when the newly tracked tool is first invoked.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one added storage write for this tool ID per persisted application state; unrelated invocations add only one Set.has while the ID remains pending.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The tracker did not track `vscode_configureAutomation`, so this one-time state update and write did not occur for that tool.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A single bounded write runs in the invocation event handler; it does not block automation execution on network, filesystem scans, IPC fan-out, or subprocess work introduced by this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost is constant for the new single tool ID; serialized set size is bounded by the static catalog's small exclusion-ID set, not invocation history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One existing listener handles tool events serially. The pending ID is deleted immediately, preventing repeated writes, and the listener disposes when all tracked IDs have been observed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Persisted invoked-tool state is restored at service construction. A warm profile where the tool was recorded skips pending tracking and the write; there is no failure retry or negative-cache loop added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor pending-set derivation and event-handler deletion/persistence directly prove the lifecycle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Underlying storage implementation latency is unmeasured, but cardinality is one and payload size is statically bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the only introduced boundary work is one bounded persistence operation tied to first use, with correct lifetime cleanup and no scaling mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and traced startup experiment resolution, tip eligibility/rendering, configuration-triggered refresh, prompt-file checks, storage persistence, and tool-invocation tracking. The change adds only fixed-cardinality catalog and assignment work; shared caching/coalescing prevents new network fan-out, and no actionable performance regression was found.
